CERILLES, RMT, MAGD Municipal Mayor Dumalinao, Zamboanga Dear Mayor Cerilles: This pertains to your letter dated 8 April 2024 concerning the Municipal Eternal Garden Project. A perusal of your letter reveals that the establishment of a Municipal Eternal Gardens has been identified as a priority project, not only as an initiative aimed at addressing the immediate need for burial space but also aligns with our long-term objectives outlined in Executive-Legislative Agenda for the years 2023-2025. Per your representation, you outlined relevant facts as follows: • • The scarcity of funds allocated for infrastructure projects led the concerned LGU to secure a loan from the Development Bank of the Philippines. However, the project implementation reportedly incurred delays due to intervals in the processing of resolutions and the lack of response from the Sangguniang Bayan. Allegedly, the discrepancy in dates between the resolutions passed and the subsequent actions taken has resulted in prolonged waiting periods, impeding the timely execution of the project. In response to the pressing need for expedited implementation of the project, the Office of the Municipal Mayor took decisive action by certifying the urgency of the matter on February 15, 2024. Allegedly, despite the efforts to underscore the urgency of the matter, the SB's response did not align with the imperative need for expeditious action. The divergence in approach resulted in unnecessary delays and hindered the Municipality's ability to address the urgent needs of its constituents effectively. Despite the follow-up letters, the Sangguniang Bayan failed to respond and acknowledge the urgency of the project. Based on the above representations, a legal advice is sought regarding the administrative liability concerning the members of the Sangguniang Bayan in the concerned municipality for their failure to respond and act on matters certified urgent by the Local Chief Executive (LCE). "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

As opined in DILG Opinion No. 52 s. 2019, the LCE has the duty to address the Sanggunian at the opening of the regular session or as may be deemed necessary to communicate to them the priority policies and programs of the LGU. Republic Act. No. 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 provides: "SECTION. 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - (a) The municipal mayor, as the chief executive of the municipal government, shall exercise such powers and perform such duties and functions as provided by this Code and other laws. (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: (1) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the municipal government, and in this connection, shall: -xxx- (iii) At the opening of the regular session of the Sangguniang Bayan for every calendar year and, as may be deemed necessary, present the program of government and propose policies and projects for the consideration of the Sangguniang Bayan as the general welfare of the inhabitants and the needs of the municipal government may require;" We reiterate that the law acknowledged the duty of the LCE to determine what will be the programs, projects or activities of the LGU, including the priority thrust of the administration. In addition, the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the LGC also recognized the power of the LCE to determine what matters will be considered urgent, VIZ: "ARTICLE 107. Ordinances and Resolutions. — The following rules shall govern the enactment of ordinances and resolutions: -xxx- (e) Any legislative matter duly certified by the local chief executive as urgent, whether or not it is included in the calendar of business, may be presented and considered by the body at the same meeting without need of suspending the rules." In DILG Opinion No. 27 s. 2009, we have the occasion to opine in this wise: "The LGC recognizes the competence of the local chief executive to certify as urgent any ordinance or resolution to be passed by the sanggunian. However, the LGC and its IRR failed to categorically specify as to what ordinances and/or resolutions should be certified as urgent. Neither is there any fixed measure or, at the very least, any instance or controlling condition that will give rise to the certification as urgent of any passage of an ordinance or resolution. The authority vested upon a local chief executive certifyinq as urqent any leqislative matter is qranted bv law in order to allow LGUs. at the instance of the local chief executive. to respond quickly. throuqh leqislative Page 2 Of 2

measures, anv exiqencv of public service. public emerqencv. or calamitv which requires immediate attention and solution. xxx Let it be noted that in the Malonzo vs. Zamora case (G.R. No. 137718, 27 July 1999), the Court pronounced that there is nothing in the law which prohibits that the three readings of a proposed ordinance be held in just one session day. Hence, the court ruled that, unlike Congress, the three readings in the sanggunian of a proposed measure could be done in one session since the law does not require that it be done on separate days." (Emphasis Supplied) We likewise reiterate this department's statement that deliberate refusal of the sanggunian to act on the proposed legislations duly certified urgent by the LCE can be a ground for dereliction of duty because the members of the sanggunians are duty bound to take immediate action on those kinds of measures for the betterment of the LGU. That duty is in accordance with Section 447 of the LGC which provides: SECTION. 447. - Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - (a) The Sangguniang Bayan, as the legislative body of the municipality, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the municipality as provided for under section 22 of this Code, and shall: (1) Approve ordinances and pass resolutions necessary for an efficient and effective municipal government, and in this connection shall: xxx We put emphasis that the administrative liabilities that will attach to erring public officials will depend on the assessment of attendant facts and circumstances, the weight of the pieces of evidence available as well as the decision of the quasi-judicial body or competent authorities before which the administrative charge/s is/are filed. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern sufficiently. Thank you. Very trul yours, BY AUTHOR TY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. OR R.
